payload.text: **THE BINARY MOVES UNDERNEATH THE TREE AND NOTHING IN THE TREE MARKS IT** (2026-09-17, d3; vc's warning, dc's measurement). `~/.local/bin/intent` and `~/.local/bin/intentd` are SYMLINKS to this checkout's own `native/rust/target/release/`, so any `cargo build --release` here replaces the binaries all four nodes are executing, mid-flight, with no commit and no file change to show for it. It is the INVERSE of a stale pair: there the tree moves ahead of an honest binary, here the tree is honest and the binary moves. So any run whose verdict depends on WHICH binary produced it pins the binary by identity and never by name -- record realpath, sha256 AND mtime at the start and again at the end, and refuse the verdict if they differ, which also leaves the banked log self-proving about what produced the result. Both readings are needed and I drove all four arms before banking: sha alone misses a rebuild producing identical bytes, mtime alone misses a swap that restores the timestamp. Copying the binary into the scratch estate pins the bytes but then costs the provenance of the copy, which is the property the log actually needs, so pinning beats copying. The hardened instrument is refs/bank/ic/0441/verify.sh and the unhardened one that produced d3 is preserved beside it at verify-as-run-d3.sh.
